answer: The protocol validates autonomous agents by reserving 1,000 distinct service slots across isolated data centers, treating each reservation as a lotus-shaped capacity lock that prohibits sharing. A verifier monitors occupancy by sending saffron-tagged packets to measure round-trip latency, ensuring every agent occupies its own wharf of bandwidth without relaying signals through pooled hardware. Honest participants pay 1x cost, while an attacker pays 1,000x for isolated slots.
